rationale: All 3 lenses ran with parseable output, spec.md was present, no decision_needed findings remain (confidence: high). 6 blocking findings: two real state bugs in the add+set-default and concurrent-toggle flows (CR-002, CR-003, CR-004), a documented accessibility-guide violation on the icon-only toggle button (CR-005), and two test-coverage gaps including a test explicitly required by spec.md's Testing section (CR-001, CR-006). 5 findings deferred as pre-existing patterns this diff only extends, not introduced by it: unencoded userId in the store URL template, unchecked API response body before showing a success toast, AddProjectPopup closing before its (now chained) onAdd resolves, an unassign-vs-set-default race on the same row, and clearDefaultProject/no-reassign-on-remove-default being out of this ticket's AC scope. 4 findings dismissed as false positives once given full context: the isAdmin->isAdmin||isMaintainer gate widen is spec-mandated (spec.md Design item 6) and backend parity was already verified and shipped in EPMCDME-15110; the flagged missing star-filled/star-outline icon assets were confirmed present on disk; the dropped setAsDefault intent on an already-assigned project is an edge-case of an edge-case with no AC coverage; and the 'rollback unverified from diff' note is a methodological observation about the pre-existing, already-relied-upon useOptimistic hook, not a defect.

findings.title: Loose default-marker test assertion
findings.problem: The test locates the badge via `closest('a, div')` and asserts on generic `querySelector('svg')` presence/absence rather than a marker-specific selector.
findings.impact: If the badge container ever renders any other icon (e.g. an external-link glyph) in the same wrapper, this test can pass or fail for the wrong reason, silently losing its AC3/AC4 coverage.
findings.recommendation: Assert on the specific star icon (e.g. a title/testid/class unique to StarFilledSvg) rather than a bare `svg` presence check.

findings.title: Swallowed set-default failure + duplicate onProjectsChange
findings.problem: `handleSetDefault` catches its own errors and never rethrows, so `await handleSetDefault(projectName)` inside `handleAddProject` always resolves. `handleSetDefault` also calls `onProjectsChange?.()` itself, and `handleAddProject` unconditionally calls it again afterward.
findings.impact: If the chained set-default call fails after a successful add, `handleAddProject` still proceeds as if the whole action succeeded (only a toast hints otherwise); on success, the parent's refetch/onProjectsChange fires twice for one user action.
findings.recommendation: Let handleSetDefault's caller decide whether to notify: only call onProjectsChange from handleAddProject's own flow, and either rethrow from handleSetDefault or return a success boolean so handleAddProject can react to a failed default-set step.

findings.title: Add+set-default chain flickers the new project's marker
findings.problem: handleSetDefault's optimistic updater runs via `useOptimistic`, whose `optimisticState` is `pendingOps` reduced over the real `state` prop (`user.projects`), not over the just-added in-memory `projects` array. Once the add's pending op resolves and is removed, the view falls back to the stale `state` prop (still missing the new project) for the instant before `handleSetDefault`'s own pending op is pushed, and that op's `.map()` runs against a list that doesn't yet contain the newly added project.
findings.impact: Contradicts the spec's explicit design goal ('no visible flicker on success' in spec.md's Data Flow section) — the newly added project's default star does not reliably show until the parent refetches via onProjectsChange.
findings.recommendation: Have handleAddProject's own optimistic updater include `is_default` on the new project synchronously when setAsDefault is true, instead of chaining a second, independent handleSetDefault call whose updater can't see the not-yet-committed new row.

findings.title: No in-flight guard on concurrent default-toggle clicks
findings.problem: Only the already-default row's toggle is disabled (`disabled={!canManageProjects || !!item.is_default}`). Nothing prevents clicking a second, different non-default row's toggle while a prior `setDefaultProject` call is still pending.
findings.impact: Two overlapping PUT requests can resolve out of order, leaving the optimistic UI showing a different default than what the backend actually persisted until the next refetch.
findings.recommendation: Track the in-flight project name (e.g. `settingDefaultFor` state) and also disable every toggle while any set-default call is pending.

findings.title: Default-toggle button has no accessible name
findings.problem: The `<button data-testid="default-toggle">` wraps only an `aria-hidden` SVG and sets `aria-pressed`, with no `aria-label` or visible text.
findings.impact: Violates .ai-run/guides/patterns/accessibility-patterns.md's blocking Pre-Delivery Checklist item ('Icon-only buttons have aria-label'); a screen-reader user has no way to learn what the control does.
findings.recommendation: Add `aria-label={item.is_default ? 'Default project' : 'Set as default project'}` (or similar) to the button.

findings.title: Missing required test: clicking the already-default row is a no-op
findings.problem: spec.md's Testing section explicitly lists this as a required case ('clicking the already-default row is a no-op'), but no test clicks a row where `item.is_default` is already true (with `canManageProjects` true) and asserts `setDefaultProject` was never called.
findings.impact: The no-op behavior is correctly implemented (`disabled={... || !!item.is_default}`) but is left unverified by the test suite, so a future refactor could silently break it without a failing test.
findings.recommendation: Add a test: render with a default project, click that row's toggle, assert `mockUserStore.setDefaultProject` is never called.
